newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman prepares for telecomms privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Oman prepares for telecomms privatisation.

text.p: Oman is preparing for the privatisation of its profitable General Telecommunication Organisation (GTO) and plans to hire consultants to help with the sell-off, the telecommunications minister said.

"With an eye on privatisation sometime in the long term, GTO plans to commission an international consultancy firm for a survey and re-evaluation of assets presently held," Minister of Posts and Telecommunications Ahmed bin Suwaidan al-Balushi said.
In an interview with Central Bank magazine al-Markazi, a copy of which was sent to Reuters on Tuesday, he said the sector would have to run on a competitive commercial basis.

"To fulfil such an aim it is planned to have the sector restructured and then proceed to establish a government stock company and then gradually offer for public participation parts of the company's capital between 10 to 15 percent at a time through the Muscat Securities Market."
"The proposed company is expected to see the light during 1997," Balushi added.
Oman, like its Gulf Arab neighbours, is trying to diversify its oil-driven economy and encourage a bigger private sector role.
